<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided `.SRCINFO` file is a metadata file used by Arch Linux's AUR to describe the package build configuration. It declares standard package attributes such as name, version, architecture, dependencies, and source URL. The source points to a release tarball hosted on GitHub at `https://github.com/sparklost/endcord-gui`, which matches the declared upstream project URL—this consistency reduces the risk of a bait-and-switch attack.

The `sha256sums = SKIP` entry indicates that the source integrity is not verified via checksum. While this is a hygiene concern because it allows for unverified downloads (and is generally discouraged), it is not inherently malicious. For binary releases like this one (a prebuilt Linux tarball), maintainers sometimes skip checksums when official hashes aren't published by upstream. However, best practice would be to verify if the upstream project provides signed checksums or reproducible builds. Despite this shortcoming, there is no evidence of active malice, obfuscated commands, unexpected network operations, or code injection in the file.

The package depends only on standard system libraries (gtk3) and optional tools (xclip, yt-dlp, etc.) that align with the application’s described functionality as a GUI Discord client with media and clipboard features. No scripts or executable logic are present in `.SRCINFO`. As a declarative metadata file, it does not execute code and cannot directly introduce supply-chain attacks. The decision remains SAFE based on absence of malicious indicators.
</details>
